name: Eerie Black
lede: Eerie Black is a near-black from Crayola's crayon list, closest in our archive to a painting's deepest shadow and present in nearly one of every five paintings we have.

sections.title: A crayon name, no earlier record
sections.body: Eerie Black is cited via Wikipedia as a name from Crayola's crayon list [1]. Its hex value, #1B1B1B, approximates RAL 9011, a graphite black from the RAL color-matching system [1]. No earlier record of the name is documented in our data [1]. Our color library's nearest look-alikes are [[black]], [[raisin-black]], [[smoky-black]] and [[rich-black-fogra39]], all within a few units of it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this near-black in 19.61 percent of the 23,781 paintings we have, 4,663 of them, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 4,329 [2]. That makes it more common than 99 percent of the named colors in our archive [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, in 68 percent of the 4,329 paintings where it appears, measured by lightness rank within each painting so varnish cannot fake it [2]. Pieter van der Werff is its most devoted painter, using it in 28 of 35 works here, four times the baseline rate of the museums those works come from [2]. The earliest match in our archive is dated 1000, nine centuries before the name's own earliest record of 1927 [2]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first, and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof the name or pigment existed that early [2].
